name: Reaiah
overview: Reaiah was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, identified as the son of Micah. His mention in Scripture is brief, focusing primarily on his lineage within the Reubenite clan. No additional personal notes or distinguishing attributes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Reaiah means 'y-h-v-h has seen,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's awareness. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 5:5 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Reaiah as the son of Micah. There is an inferred relationship to Baal as his father, though this is less certain. Beyond these, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Reaiah's significance lies in his identification as a descendant within the tribe of Reuben, contributing to the genealogical records that preserve the heritage of Israel. His mention underscores the importance of family lines in God's providential plan, even when individual details are limited. This genealogy serves to affirm the continuity of God's people through successive generations.
